request.spec:
Grades can be added (an entry and a button; GRADE_ADDED grade=<grade>): a code of one to three
capital letters not yet a grade; anything else is refused. A new grade appears in every grade
select, the summary, the rates and the rate calendar.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Grades can be added (an entry and a button; GRADE_ADDED grade=<grade>): a code of one to three
capital letters not yet a grade; anything else is refused. A new grade appears in every grade
select, the summary, the rates and the rate calendar.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grades can now be added. `bin/e2e` passes 3 of its 4 tests; "grades editable scenario 1" still fails on one check that I believe was already broken before my change.

**The failing check:** scenario 1 expects `person-excess` to show `0.00` for Ada, but the app shows `45.00`. In that scenario Ada's pool cut is 50.00 and the sheet's cap is 5.00. The app's existing rule counts the cut toward the excess, so 50.00 − 5.00 = 45.00. None of that code (excess, pool cuts, cap) depends on grades, and I didn't change it. To check that nothing else was hiding behind it, I ran a temporary copy of scenario 1 with only the `person-excess` checks removed. It passed, including all the grade checks and the audit lines. I deleted that copy afterwards. I couldn't run the app as it was before my change, because there is no git history to go back to. Making this test pass would mean changing how excess is worked out, which this request doesn't cover, so I've left it alone.

**What changed:**
- **Adding a grade:** a new entry and button on the Grades panel (`grade-add-code`, `grade-add`). A code of one to three capital letters that isn't already a grade is added; surrounding spaces are trimmed, so " XY " becomes XY. Anything else shows `grade-error` and writes nothing. A successful add writes `GRADE_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> grade=<grade>` to the audit file.
- **Stored data:** a new migration (`V123__grade.sql`) adds a per-sheet table of added grades. It also widens the existing grade columns, which only held one character, so codes like XY fit.
- **Server:** every sheet still has A, B and C, followed by its added grades in the order they were added. Grade checks used to accept only A, B or C. They now accept any code of one to three capital letters, and adding a person, editing a grade, setting a rate, importing rates, bulk grading, retiring or merging now refuses a grade the sheet doesn't have. The per-grade settings in the settings response now cover the added grades. A default grade that isn't on the sheet falls back to A.
- **Front end:** the grade selects on the person form, the inline and bulk grade controls, the rate form and rate preview now use the sheet's own grade list. So do the summary, current rates, rate calendar, consolidated totals and sheet comparison. The settings form now accepts any of the sheet's grades as the default grade.

**Not covered:** the per-grade inputs on the settings form (terms, grace days, proof threshold, clerk limit per grade) still show only A, B and C, and the server still accepts dated values for those settings only for A, B and C.
